newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian sought in connection with polls boycott.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian sought in connection with polls boycott.

text.p: Indonesian police on Wednesday were hunting for a man suspected of encouraging residents in a Central Java town to boycott last Thursday's general elections.

"We are still looking for the man, Darsono. He is suspected of encouraging people in the Kedungombo area, near Boyolali in Central Java, not to vote in the elections," a police officer in Boyolali told Reuters by telephone.
He declined to give other details.

The Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Wednesday that Darsono had been accused of encouraging more than 250 people in Kedungombo, about 250 km (156 miles) east of Jakarta, to join the ranks of the Golput.
Golput, which literally means White Group, is an informal grouping of people who spoil their ballots or abstain from voting as a protest against the government.
Failing to vote is not a crime in Indonesia, but government leaders had threatened during the election campaign to take action against anyone who encouraged a boycott of the polls.

President Suharto's ruling Golkar party won more than 74 percent of the vote for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives in polls held every five years, up from 68 percent in the 1992 general election.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) won almost 23 percent, up from 17 percent. The share of the only other legal party, the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), plunged to three percent from 15 percent.
Final election results will be issued on June 17.
